rules.title: Cambridge Fair Housing Ordinance prohibits housing discrimination based on source of income
rules.requirement: In Cambridge housing transactions, landlords, sellers, and rental agents may not discriminate based on source of income, which includes Section 8 and public benefits. The ordinance covers rental decisions and tenancy terms, while allowing reasonable selection standards if applied equally and uniformly to all applicants.
rules.key_value: Source of income is a protected category in housing discrimination law
rules.stage_quote:
The Commission enforces two ordinances: the
Cambridge Human Rights Ordinance, chapter 2.76
and the
Cambridge Fair Housing Ordinance, chapter 14.04
.

rules.penalty: The Commission has the authority to provide various remedies after hearing, including filing a criminal complaint in District Court, levying civil fines of up to $300 for each violation, filing a civil complaint in Superior Court seeking injunctive relief, and seeking an award of damages, expenses and other relief.
rules.rule_quote:
The protected categories under the Cambridge Human Rights Ordinance and the Cambridge Fair Housing Ordinance are the following:
Disability – Defined consistent with the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) – a physical or mental impairment which substantially limits one or more major life activities
Race
Color
National Origin or Ancestry
Family Status
Source of Income, includes Section 8 and public benefits
